messages:
Ian Park: Customer reported intermittent TLS failures after our rotator redeploy ~2h ago. Some of their clients see "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" while others connect fine. Seen from multiple regions. Attach logs below. 

Ian Park: customer logs:
```
TLS handshake error: remote error: tls: handshake failure
x509: certificate signed by unknown authority (verify error)
```

Priya Nair: Oof, do we know whether customer is using pinned intermediates or a custom truststore? :thinking: Also are they behind a private ALB or using our edge?

Ian Park: They said Private VPC with their own client apps (some mobile, some server). They mentioned they pin the intermediate in their truststore. Not sure about OCSP stapling.

Maria Gomez: Can we check rotator bundle that went live at deployment? deploy-bot shows rotator v2.3.4 rolled at 1759001020. There's a chance the bundle got re-ordered or an extra cross-signed cert slipped in.

deploy-bot: rotator v2.3.4 deployed by @maria at 1759001020, bundle checksum sha256: abcdef123456

Jonah Li: Quick triage steps for support to ask customer (and we should reproduce):
1) Run openssl to inspect presented chain:
```
openssl s_client -connect customer-vip.example.com:443 -servername api.customer.example.com -showcerts
```
2) If they pin intermediate, check order and serials in the chain. Order should be leaf -> intermediate(s) -> root (not included normally).
3) Capture curl verbose output to see if OCSP fetches are timing out:
```
curl -v https://api.customer.example.com/ --resolve api.customer.example.com:443:IP
```

Maria Gomez: If openssl shows intermediate cert AFTER the leaf but with wrong issuer order (or missing intermediate entirely) that's our rotator packing bug. But if intermediate is present and ordered, maybe their client enforces AIA/OCSP and can't reach OCSP responder from their environment (egress allowlist).

Priya Nair: Also ask customer to run this command from a failing client host: 
```
python -c "import ssl,socket; s=ssl.create_default_context(); print(s.get_ca_certs())"
```
(we just want to know if their truststore contains intermediate and which one)

Ian Park: I grabbed rotator upload artifacts. The uploaded bundle shows 3 certs, but the concatenation order differs from the previous bundle (leaf, cross-signed intermediate, canonical intermediate). Could that confuse some clients?

Jonah Li: Yes — some TLS stacks will reject if chain uses a cross-signed intermediate with unexpected issuer ordering, especially if client pins a specific intermediate cert fingerprint. Two paths to mitigate quickly:
- Re-roll the rotator bundle with canonical intermediate first (preserve old order used prior to deploy) and push a hotfix.
- Ask customer to relax pinning (temporary) or add the cross-signed intermediate to their truststore.

Maria Gomez: Also validate that our edge/haproxy/ALB is not stripping or reordering certs on SNI passthrough. I know a past bug re-serialized certs on TLS termination. Check haproxy config and any reloads around 1759001000.

Priya Nair: For next steps I recommend we: 1) Request s_client output + curl verbose from customer 2) Attach rotator bundle checksum & uploaded file to the ticket 3) Prepare a rollback bundle (old checksum) to test quickly in staging and offer that to the customer if rollback fixes it.

Ian Park: I'll collect customer's s_client output and paste here. If we confirm bundle order mismatch we'll coordinate a hotfix rollback and ping affected customers.

Priya Nair: Adding to ticket and paging eng-oncall if we see widespread impact. Tagging @Maria and @Jonah. :white_check_mark:
